THE PREMISE OF THE ESCALATION IS THEREFORE IN DOUBT ON ITS FIRST LIMB (no allowlisted locator) AND THIS BATCH TESTS ITS SECOND LIMB, WHICH IS THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS: is Article 1110 served there in VISIBLE PROSE, i.e. in a content type from which excerpt_of can produce any text at all (scripts/fetch_relay.py:124 returns the empty string for every content type that is neither html nor text). THE ANALYST'S OWN PRIOR, STATED BEFORE THE ROWS RETURN AND AGAINST ITS OWN INTEREST: this batch probably comes back NEGATIVE, on either of two independent grounds. (a) HOST. investmentpolicy.unctad.org has answered this relay 403 on every row since 2026-08-10; its last outcome 'ok' was 2026-08-09-daily.json. 12 refused/403 rows, 15 ok rows, all ok rows on or before 2026-08-09. A 403 today is a TOOL-LAYER OUTCOME and says nothing about whether Article 1110 is served at that URL. (b) CONTENT TYPE. This repository's own record already characterises a sibling locator of exactly this shape - https://investmentpolicy.unctad.org/international-investment-agreements/treaty-files/736/download , cited at analytics/insights.jsonl line 28 and STATE_OF_THE_ANSWER.md:941 - as a 'primary PDF not directly read'. If /treaty-files/NNNN/download serves application/pdf, then excerpt_of returns the empty string, no find can reach it, and the honest answer to the chairman's question is: a locator exists at an allowlisted host, but NOT in visible prose. NOTE that no relay row has ever been fired at any UNCTAD treaty-files path: grep over analytics/fetch-requests/ and analytics/fetch-results/ for 'treaty-files' returns 0. The PDF characterisation above is the record's own description, not this project's retrieval. THAT is what row 3 settles, and it settles it whichever way it falls. PAIRING DISCIPLINE (README, the 2026-09-17 lesson). Every URL in this batch that could produce a null carries a companion row on the SAME URL in the SAME run with find:"" - which returns the head excerpt and, more importantly, returns content_type and bytes REGARDLESS of whether any find would match (scripts/fetch_relay.py:172 and :177). A find:"" row is therefore never itself a null-producing row: it is the instrument window that makes its siblings' nulls readable. WHAT EACH ROW MEANS, PRE-REGISTERED. ROW 1 (https://investmentpolicy.unctad.org/international-investment-agreements/treaties/bit/3104/nafta-1992-, find "") - the NAFTA Navigator treaty page, docket-page-before-document-hunt. HIT (outcome ok, content_type text/html, non-empty excerpt): the host answers this relay today at this path, the tag-strip yields prose, and row 2's null is readable. MISS (empty excerpt on an ok row): the page rendered no prose after tag-stripping, and row 2 is uninterpretable. REFUSED/403 or robots_disallowed: instrument, not resource; rows 1-2 say nothing and the 2026-08-10 403 regime is confirmed to extend to a path never tried. ROW 2 (https://investmentpolicy.unctad.org/international-investment-agreements/treaties/bit/3104/nafta-1992-, find "Chapter Eleven") - does the Navigator's own NAFTA page name its Chapter Eleven file in visible prose. HIT: UNCTAD's NAFTA entry itself associates the treaty with a Chapter Eleven document, which upgrades the S1/S2/S4 title evidence from an engine's index to the database's own page. MISS (with row 1 hitting): the association between the NAFTA entry and treaty-file 2413 rests on engine titles alone and must be reported that way. ROW 3 (https://investmentpolicy.unctad.org/international-investment-agreements/treaty-files/2413/download, find "") - THE DECISIVE ROW OF THE BATCH, and the cheapest. It returns content_type and bytes whatever the body is. content_type application/pdf: NAFTA Chapter 11 is NOT served in visible prose at this allowlisted host, no find can reach it, and the escalation SURVIVES on its operative limb - but with a materially better locator for the operator (https, on an allowlisted host, and titled 'NAFTA Chapter 11' by the engine) than the http-only sice.oas.org page whose service of Article 1110 nobody has established. content_type text/html or text/plain WITH a non-empty excerpt: the escalation's premise FAILS, this council can read NAFTA Chapter 11 through its own relay, and rows 4-6 become readable. REFUSED/403: instrument, not resource; the question is unanswered and nothing about NAFTA may be inferred. ROW 4 (https://investmentpolicy.unctad.org/international-investment-agreements/treaty-files/2413/download, find "Article 1110") - is the expropriation article carried in the served prose. HIT: the 400-character window centred on the FIRST occurrence enters the record as a quotable retrieved body (relay excerpts are obtainable bodies under the council's quotation rule); expect that first occurrence to be a heading or a table-of-contents line rather than operative text. MISS, WITH ROW 3 SHOWING PROSE: the string is absent from the served stream - a real negative about this document, not about NAFTA. MISS WITH ROW 3 SHOWING application/pdf or a 403: uninterpretable, and will be reported as uninterpretable. ROW 5 (https://investmentpolicy.unctad.org/international-investment-agreements/treaty-files/2413/download, find "intellectual property") - the research question's rigid designator, used as a NEUTRAL probe. It is deliberately NOT a phrase recalled from the provision under test: this council does not design a find out of model knowledge of the text it is trying to read, because a hit on such a string would be self-fulfilling. HIT: the window shows the first context in which Chapter Eleven's served prose speaks of intellectual property, which is direct evidence bearing on whether the chapter contains any IP-specific language at all. MISS with row 3 showing prose: Chapter Eleven's served stream does not contain the phrase, which would itself be a finding about the seed treaty's expropriation chapter. ROW 6 (https://investmentpolicy.unctad.org/international-investment-agreements/treaty-files/2413/download, find "Article 1111") - the tail-of-1110 window. excerpt_of starts the window 100 characters BEFORE the first match (scripts/fetch_relay.py:134-135), so a hit on the NEXT article's designator returns the prose immediately preceding it - which, in body text, is the LAST paragraph of Article 1110, the position where a paragraph (7) would sit. This is the only row in the batch that could bear on the paragraph-7 question itself. CAVEAT REGISTERED IN ADVANCE: if the document has a table of contents, the first 'Article 1111' will be in it and the window will show a TOC line, not the end of Article 1110 - which is readable as such and is not a failure. NOTHING ABOUT PARAGRAPH 7 WILL BE ASSERTED FROM A TOC WINDOW. ROW 7 (https://investmentpolicy.unctad.org/international-investment-agreements/treaty-files/2542/download, find "") - the sibling candidate, returned by S1 and S2 under the title '11-1 CHAPTER ELEVEN INVESTMENT Section A: Investment'. One diagnostic row only. Its head excerpt and content type say whether this is a second Chapter Eleven file and, if it is text, which agreement it belongs to. It is NOT assumed to be NAFTA: two engine titles beginning '11-1' is a lead, not an identification, and a screen licenses a question and nothing else. ROW 8 (https://example.com/, find "Example Domain") - the CLOSING BRACKET control, and it is a different control from the one the relay prepends automatically (scripts/fetch_relay.py:199 fetches https://example.com/ with no find). The prepended row proves reachability; THIS row proves the find path itself executed on this run, because it is a find this council knows must match. If this row misses while the prepended control is ok, every null in the batch is an instrument null and the batch carries no information about any resource. WHAT THIS BATCH CANNOT DO, STATED UP FRONT. Even on a complete success it does not print NAFTA Article 1110 paragraph 7 into this record: four hundred characters do not hold an article. What a success buys is the discharge of a CHANNEL question - whether this council can read its own seed treaty's expropriation chapter at all - and, on row 6, at most one window onto the article's tail.
